question: In the combined dataset that unifies the trees data with the income data by ZIP code, filling missing ZIP values where necessary, which three boroughs, restricted to records with median and mean income both greater than zero and a valid borough name, contain the highest number of trees, and what is the average mean income for each of these three boroughs?
sql:
WITH filtered_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t.boroname,
        t.zipcode,
        i.Estimate_Mean_income
    FROM trees t
    FULL OUTER JOIN income_trees i ON t.zipcode = i.zipcode
    WHERE i.Estimate_Median_income > 0 
        AND i.Estimate_Mean_income > 0
        AND t.boroname IS NOT NULL
),
borough_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        boroname,
        COUNT(*) as tree_count
    FROM filtered_data
    GROUP BY boroname
),
top3_boroughs AS (
    SELECT boroname
    FROM borough_counts
    ORDER BY tree_count DESC
    LIMIT 3
),
results AS (
    SELECT 
        f.boroname,
        AVG(f.Estimate_Mean_income) as avg_mean_income
    FROM filtered_data f
    JOIN top3_boroughs t ON f.boroname = t.boroname
    GROUP BY f.boroname
    ORDER BY tree_count DESC
),
with_tree_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        f.boroname,
        COUNT(*) as tree_count,
        AVG(f.Estimate_Mean_income) as avg_mean_income
    FROM filtered_data f
    JOIN top3_boroughs t ON f.boroname = t.boroname
    GROUP BY f.boroname
)
SELECT boroname, tree_count, avg_mean_income FROM with_tree_counts ORDER BY tree_count DESC
